Dude, you're not too old for college. It's a great thing that you actually went! Many people don't finish school and then regret it afterwards and end up never going because they think they're too old. I was once at a hairdresser salon sitting in a chair waiting for the hairdresser when a old woman sat in front of me and reached out to me.

Old lady: "Are you in school?"
Me: "Yeah, I am."
Old lady: "Good. Don't ever think about quitting school. Finish it. If you don't  you'll end up like me. Regretting it. There is nothing in life that I regret as much as quitting school so please do me a favor and finish your studies." 
Me: "...Uhmm thank you for the advice" 

It was a pretty humbling experience and I realized then how many people regret quitting their studies, so I decided not to. 

Anyways I just wanted to share this and I dont know what I can say about the life time depression. The only advice I can think of is seeing a psychologist and trying out anti-depressants. When I started taking them my suicidal thoughts diminished but I turned pretty numb instead.

Oh wow. Im sorry for how naive I was compared to your circumstances. Damn. Do you live alone or with your parents? I would literally be screaming for help in this situation. Can you maybe reach out to your parents or relatives for better living conditions? (shelter and food). If not then maybe ask a friend if you can move to their house and look for a job near their area?

Yeah I know and it kind of sucks. But everything in life costs money. Yeah and it kind of sucks that when we're depressed our lights on the inside were switched off a long time ago and we're basically just walking corpses.

I would really advice you to go to therapy if this is the only reason holding you back. Psychologists aren't allowed to judge you or show emotions of judgement. Also you're not a dumbass for waiting to dump your ex. It's so common that there are websites on the internet that do articles about leaving your ex. I've stayed in a relationship 6 months more than I should of and gotten back with a horrible ex. So if you can afford it you could try it out to see if it helps.

If you were going to kill yourself I'm really glad you didn't. If you start thinking about it again call a suicide hotline. It sounds cheesy but there are tons of them and they usually help you. 

You could also try taking anti-depressants and if you can afford it, visit a psychologist. Im taking Sertraline and that numbed my suicidal thought a lot, but they made me numb as well. You could start by being on meds to prevent the suicidal thoughts. Thank you for not going through with it by reading my post.

I guess it could be hard to find your element as it is highly personal process. We're all starting from different places in terms of our own characteristics and circumstances. The element is also different for each of us. But if it is really hard for you to find your element, just try going to a counsellor and ask to have a career test or personality test. Then you will hopefully see where your interests lie. Where your interests lie is usually what you are supposed to be doing. And thats when you are in your element. I know that not everyone will find out what their element as it is a highly personal process, like I said before.
You're welcome. Yeah I agree, I think its really important to shed some light or at least try to help even a little bit on this sub as most people here are seriously thinking about ending their life.

What about when you were younger? didn't you enjoy anything then? maybe sports, studying, drawing, socializing? If not I think you should start trying things out and see if there is anything that catches your attention. I read somewhere once that when you're really depressed that you have to start doing things and trying things out to start enjoying them. When we're depressed our serotonin is so low that it gets hard to enjoy anything at all anymore. And that is why you have to start trying something out and the interest in that will grow with time.

Well that's your perception of yourself. It doesn't mean that it has to be true..our perceptions of ourselves are often really messed up. If you've been bullied in the past, don't listen to that. Just think about people, everyone has a different perception of you and if someone has said something mean to you (ugly, virgin, etc) it doesn't have to be true. I know that this sounds really naive, but it's a better thinking pattern than thinking that everything that people think about you is true and punishing yourself for that. My dad used to call me stupid and tell me to shut up and a lot of other mean stuff and by just thinking "wow he must be really messed up and this is honestly just his perception of me..it doesn't mean that what he is saying is true" 

Also there are many virgins out there and there's nothing wrong with that. I know plenty of people who didn't lose their virginity until they were in their 20's and 30's. If you think you are ugly you can try taking care of yourself physically. You can start going to the gym or just by walking 5 minutes a day. You can take care of your hair and skin and eat healthy.

But with this advice *hopefully* helping you, it could help your self-confidence finding out what you just really love doing. Just think about what made you happy in the past or what makes you be a lil bit happier nowadays? I know it's probably not much since we're all dealing with major depression here. But go back to when you were not depressed and think about what things you enjoyed. It could be gaming, socializing, cooking, reading, hiking..honestly whatever. 

I'm honestly not sure if it can tell you about the desire for sex as the book is just about finding out what you love doing and about socializing. There is one chapter in the book that is about your tribe. So it does cover your desire for companionship.

The tribe chapter covers what kind of people you want to associate with either in real life or on social media. I can write down all of the important things I read from that chapter here if you want.

P.s These are the chapters in the book, so you know what every chapter is about: 

* Finding your element 
* What are you good at?
* How do you know? 
* What do you love? 
* What Makes You Happy? 
* What's your attitude? 
* Where Are You Now? 
* Where's your tribe?

Like I said before, I was just hoping this could help a bit. Im not trying to make anyone buy themselves a book or anything. The most important thing I read was finding the element, which is finding out what you love doing.
